page: Amazon Web Services i7i.48xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by the Nitro hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It features dedicated Intel Xeon 8559C processors running at 3.2 GHz, delivering 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is a key highlight, consisting of 45000 GB of bundled NVMe SSD capacity, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the i7i.48xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance across multiple domains. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests ranks in the top 10%, aided by advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached large-block reads is highly efficient, placing in the top tier. Database operations, including Redis SET benchmarks and Passmark database tests, also achieve top-tier status, reflecting the high throughput of the local NVMe storage and memory subsystem.

Given its massive 45 TB local NVMe storage, high memory capacity, and 100 Gbps network baseline, this server is designed for data-intensive, high-throughput workloads. It is highly cost-efficient for large-scale database deployments, real-time analytics, and caching layers that require massive local storage density and high memory bandwidth without the overhead of external storage. The absence of a GPU makes it less suitable for heavy graphics rendering, though its AMX instructions support efficient CPU-based LLM inference.
